subject: TideGate: must-have model residency + audit snapshot — feasibility ask
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@tidegate.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TideGate: must-have model residency + audit snapshot — feasibility ask

Hi Irene/Jonas,

Quick background: TideGate is moving fast toward a pilot with a regulated payments product. Procurement explicitly listed two "go/no-go" items in the security questionnaire that are blocking signature: (1) guaranteed per-account model residency / affinity (they want the same model variant pinned to their tenant for audit reproducibility), and (2) deterministic KV-cache snapshot exports (they need an encrypted, time-stamped snapshot per day for auditors).

They labeled both as MUST-HAVE for their initial production cutover. Sarah (copied) just sent over a scoped list — attaching tidegate_requirements_v1.pdf.

Ask: can Product + Eng provide a feasibility read (technical blockers, rough engineering lead time, and recommended minimum contract terms to justify the work — e.g., reserved capacity months, SOW, or premium SLA)? We need an internal recommendation by EOD Friday so we can put a firm date in the mutual action plan.

Possible trade-offs to consider:
- offer a micro-SLA and a pinned quantized variant instead of full-precision model residency
- deliver a daily snapshot (vs continuous stream) for first phase

Next steps I propose: quick triage spike, then a scoped implementation / canary plan if feasible.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: tidegate_requirements_v1.pdf (summary of audit asks)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@tidegate.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TideGate: must-have model residency + audit snapshot — feasibility ask

Thanks Monica — I skimmed the attachment and the two asks are clear. A few clarifying questions before I commit to timeline:

1) By "per-account model residency" do they require exclusive GPU residency (physical pinning) or logical affinity (traffic routed to the same model variant instance across requests)?
2) What retention + export cadence do auditors require for the KV snapshots (daily, hourly, retention window)?
3) Are they asking for exports containing user prompts/outputs or only model metadata + token-level logs (redacted traces)?

Initial thoughts:
- Logical model affinity with a pinned model version is much faster to implement (routing + tenancy policies) than exclusive hardware residency.
- Deterministic KV snapshots: engineering can produce a daily encrypted export of the KV state and metadata, but reproducing exact token-level generation determinism is non-trivial unless we standardize model variants and internal seeds.

If they truly need full reproducibility (byte-for-byte), this could be a 6–10 week effort (spike + hardened delivery) and will likely require reserved capacity and a security review. If they accept a pinned model variant + daily snapshot of metadata and cache state, we can probably scope a 3–4 week build with a small spike first.

Jonas — can you and infra weigh in with a quick estimate? If we agree on an approach, I can scope the product requirements doc and propose an MVP canary plan to TideGate.

Thanks,
Irene

--

Group Product Manager, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@tidegate.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TideGate: must-have model residency + audit snapshot — feasibility ask

On Wed, Jun 5, 2028 at 12:08 PM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial thoughts:
> - Logical model affinity with a pinned model version is much faster to implement (routing + tenancy policies) than exclusive hardware residency.

Short answer: yes, logical affinity + pinned model version is implementable quickly. Notes from infra/serving perspective:

- Work needed:
  * Routing policy: tenant->model-version affinity table + fallback rules (2–3 engineer-weeks if we leverage existing routing flags).
  * KV snapshot export: capture KV namespace per-tenant, serialize with timestamp, sign/encrypt via KMS. Small job (1–2 engineer-weeks) + storage lifecycle.
  * Deterministic replay: to guarantee identical outputs we need to freeze runtime seeds, kernel ordering, and quantization masks. That is a much larger scope — estimate 6–10 weeks and requires test harness for bit-exact verification.

- Dependencies & risks:
  * Reserved capacity: if TideGate wants strict latency and affinity guarantees, we should require a Dedicated pool reservation (monthly commit) — otherwise affinity is soft and can be evicted under load.
  * Security/compliance: KV snapshots will contain sensitive metadata — we need a legal/compliance sign-off and a planned SOC2/pen test checklist item.

Recommendation (practical MVP):
1) Spike (1 week): prototype routing + snapshot export for a single tenant (dev-only) to validate pipeline and KMS integration (INF-8271).
2) MVP (3 weeks): production routing table, daily encrypted snapshot exports to tenant-owned S3 (or our secure bucket with cross-account access), and a documented fallback (soft affinity).
3) Phase 2 (optional): deterministic replay (6–10 weeks) if TideGate insists on byte-for-byte reproduction.

I'll open a short-lived Jira for the spike and attach preliminary tasks.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@tidegate.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-06T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TideGate: must-have model residency + audit snapshot — feasibility ask

Thanks all for the fast responses. A few clarifications from our security/compliance team (they're on CC on procurement mailbox):

- Affinity: logical affinity + pinned model version is acceptable for the first release as long as the contract commits to a documented process + notice period if you need to evict or change the pinned variant.
- Snapshots: daily encrypted exports containing the KV state and model metadata are sufficient for auditors. We do not need token-level transcripts for Phase 1 — metadata + KV + model-version stamps are fine.
- Reproducibility: we understand byte-for-byte replay is heavy; we will treat Phase 2 as separate.

I attached tidegate_audit_scope.xlsx with the fields our auditors expect. Procurement is prepared to discuss a 12-month reserved capacity commitment if we can get an agreed MVP timeline and an SLA for affinity disruptions (e.g., 99.9% affinity uptime).

Can Mona (monica) and team please formalize an action plan (spike deadline, canary window, owner list) so procurement can move forward with terms?

Best,
Sarah

Director, Cloud Integrations | TideGate Financial

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Action items I will drive with suggested owners & dates:

1) Spike (1 week) — owner: Jonas; target: prototype routing + one-day snapshot export to a test bucket. Target complete: 2028-06-14.
2) Product PRD (MVP) — owner: Irene; target: include acceptance criteria, data handling, exported schema, and contract language for affinity SLA. Draft due: 2028-06-12.
3) Procurement alignment & sketch SOW — owner: Monica; target: draft SOW and reserved capacity ask (12 months) for TideGate to review by 2028-06-18.
4) Compliance pre-check & red-team flags — owner: Security/Compliance (I'll loop them once PRD is ready).

Jonas: please create the Jira (INF-8271 is fine) and link the spike ticket in the HubSpot deal. Irene: once PRD draft is ready, I'll schedule a 30-min alignment call with TideGate's procurement and compliance.

If we hit the spike milestones I will get procurement to sign a letter of intent for the reserved pool to cover Phase 1.

Thanks — Monica
